fantasy: Being effortlessly in the groove. The player should feel skilled slightly before they actually are.
core_loop: Hear the beat → anticipate the next gate → tap to switch lanes on the beat → combo climbs and the track responds → miss, and the run ends → retry immediately.
pillars: The beat is always right — a miss must read as the player's error, never the game's
Readable at a glance on a phone held one-handed

prototype: Yandex SDK init and rewarded stub

out_of_scope.why_excluded: One track proves the mechanic. More tracks are content, and content does not answer the validation question.
No bearing on whether beat-matching feels fair, which is the only thing at issue.
Adds backend and moderation surface for a retention effect the personal best already supplies at this scope.
A 240-second session has no room to present and complete one — see design rule short_session_no_daily_quest.

scope.progression_terminal: Progression is the personal best. There is no terminal state and the loop is deliberately open, bounded by a single track.

session.structure: A run lasts 45-90 seconds and ends on a miss. A session is a string of runs, each starting within a second of the last ending. The session ends when the player beats their best or stops improving — both are satisfying stopping points rather than arbitrary ones.
session.end_condition: Player sets a new personal best, or three runs pass without improvement.

retention.return_reason: They know they can beat their own score, and they were close last time.
retention.progression_loop: Score ceiling rises with familiarity rather than with unlocks. The player improves; the game does not change.

placements.trigger: On a miss that ends a run above the player's median score
placements.player_value: Continue the run from the missed gate, keeping the combo

placements.trigger: Between runs, at most once every 180 seconds, never inside a run
placements.player_value: None — this is a pure interruption and is priced as such, kept below the platform cadence limit

monetization.economy: No currency. The rewarded continue is the only economic action.

progression: There is no unlock progression. The player's skill is the progression, and the score is its readout.
difficulty: Three ramps differing in gate density and tempo. The first ramp is deliberately forgiving for the first 20 seconds so a new player reaches a reward before failing.
controls: Single tap anywhere switches lanes. No other input.

ux.onboarding: No tutorial. The first 10 seconds present one gate at a slow tempo with a pulsing prompt; the control teaches itself because the idiom is already familiar on this portal.
screens: Fail with retry and rewarded continue
ux.accessibility: Beat is signalled visually as well as audibly, so the game is playable muted — which also covers the substantial share of portal traffic that plays with sound off.

art_direction: Flat neon vectors on dark ground. Procedurally generated, near-zero asset cost, and the palette shifts with the combo so visual feedback is free.
audio_direction: One licensed loop at a fixed BPM. Fixed tempo is a design constraint, not a simplification: variable tempo multiplies the latency problem that is already the title's main risk.

platform_constraints_applied.requirement: Russian localization required, machine translation rejected
platform_constraints_applied.how_addressed: ru is in scope.locales and budgeted for human translation; text is kept to under 40 strings to make this cheap.

platform_constraints_applied.requirement: Loading progress must be reported through the SDK
platform_constraints_applied.how_addressed: Loading screen is driven by the SDK loading API rather than a fake progress bar.
Interstitial cadence set to 180s, comfortably above the limit and matched to session structure.
Same 180s cadence satisfies the tighter of the two limits, so one build serves both.

rule_results.note: Session 240s exceeds the tightest platform interval of 180s.

rule_results.measured: open loop, bounded by one track

open_questions: What is the actual audio-to-input latency on a mid-range Android phone in Chrome? This is the title's central risk and the prototype exists mainly to answer it.
Does a fixed-tempo track become monotonous within a 240-second session?
